questions.prompt:
\(x=8a(b+9)\)

The given equation relates the positive numbers \(a\), \(b\), and \(x\). Which equation correctly expresses \(a\) in terms of \(b\) and \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
To isolate \(a\), divide both sides of the equation by \(8(b+9)\). Because \(b\) is positive, \(b+9\) is not zero, so this division is allowed. This gives \(\frac{x}{8(b+9)}=a\), or \(a=\frac{x}{8(b+9)}\).

\(a=\frac{x}{8}-(b+9)\) subtracts \((b+9)\) instead of dividing by it; it is equivalent to \(x=8(a+b+9)\). \(a=\frac{8(b+9)}{x}\) is the reciprocal of the correct expression; it is equivalent to \(x=\frac{8(b+9)}{a}\). \(a=8x(b+9)\) multiplies instead of dividing; it is equivalent to \(x=\frac{a}{8(b+9)}\).

questions.prompt: A line segment that has a length of 115 centimeters (cm) is divided into three parts. One part is 47 cm long. The other two parts have lengths that are equal to each other. What is the length, in cm, of one of the other two parts of equal length?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) represent the length, in cm, of each of the two equal parts. The three parts add up to the total, so \(47+x+x=115\), or \(47+2x=115\). Subtracting 47 from each side gives \(2x=68\), and dividing each side by 2 gives \(x=34\). So each of the two equal parts is 34 cm.

questions.prompt:
\(p(x)+57=x^2\)

The given equation relates the value of \(x\) and its corresponding value of \(p(x)\) for the function \(p\). What is the minimum value of the function \(p\)?
questions.explanation:
Subtracting 57 from both sides gives \(p(x)=x^2-57\). This is in the form \(p(x)=a(x-r)^2+s\) with \(a=1>0\), \(r=0\) and \(s=-57\); when \(a>0\), the minimum value is \(s\). Because \(x^2\) is never negative and equals 0 when \(x=0\), the smallest value of \(p(x)\) is \(-57\).

Wrong choices: \(-3249\) results from squaring 57; \(57\) has the wrong sign (moving \(+57\) to the other side changes its sign); \(3249\) results from squaring 57.

questions.prompt: If \(k-x\) is a factor of the expression \(-x^2+\frac{1}{29}nk^2\), where \(n\) and \(k\) are constants and \(k>0\), what is the value of \(n\)?
questions.explanation:
If \(k-x\) is a factor of a polynomial in \(x\), then the polynomial equals 0 when \(k-x\) equals 0, that is, when \(x=k\). Substituting \(k\) for \(x\) gives \(-k^2+\frac{1}{29}nk^2=0\). Because \(k>0\), \(k^2\neq 0\), so dividing by \(k^2\) gives \(-1+\frac{1}{29}n=0\). Solving, \(n=29\).

Check: with \(n=29\), the expression becomes \(-x^2+k^2\), a difference of squares that has \(k-x\) as a factor. Each other choice leaves a nonzero value when \(x=k\), so \(k-x\) would not be a factor.

If \(2k-x\) is a factor of a polynomial in \(x\), then the polynomial equals 0 when \(2k-x\) equals 0, that is, when \(x=2k\). Substituting \(2k\) for \(x\) gives \(-\left(2k\right)^2+\frac{1}{12}nk^2=0\), which simplifies to \(-4k^2+\frac{1}{12}nk^2=0\). Because \(k>0\), \(k^2\neq 0\), so dividing by \(k^2\) gives \(-4+\frac{1}{12}n=0\). Solving, \(n=48\).

Check: with \(n=48\), the expression becomes \(-x^2+4k^2\), a difference of squares that has \(2k-x\) as a factor. Each other choice leaves a nonzero value when \(x=2k\), so \(2k-x\) would not be a factor.

questions.prompt:
\(5(x+7)=15(x-17)(x+7)\)

What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(5(x+7)\) from each side: \(0=15(x-17)(x+7)-5(x+7)\). Factor out the common factor \((x+7)\): \(0=(x+7)\left(15(x-17)-5\right)\), which simplifies to \(0=(x+7)(15x-260)\).

A product is 0 when a factor is 0, so \(x=-7\) or \(x=\frac{52}{3}\). The sum of the solutions is \(-7+\left(\frac{52}{3}\right)=\frac{31}{3}\). Examples of ways to enter a correct answer: 31/3, 10.33.

Watch out: dividing both sides by \((x+7)\) at the start loses the solution \(x=-7\).
